box-header.title: What an ACME certificate is and is not

label.text: An ACME certificate proves control of the domain name and nothing about who runs it. It is free, issued in seconds, short-lived, and depends on renewal working and on the authority being reachable and within its rate limits. It comes with no support and no warranty.

Another certificate is the better choice where more assurance is wanted: an organization-validated or extended-validation certificate for ecommerce, where the authority has checked the business; a certificate under a support contract for a high-volume or high-reliability site; a wildcard; a company's own authority for inside names; a certificate a partner pins. Those are files in runtime/cert (name.crt and name.key, or certbot's name/fullchain.pem and privkey.pem), and they show here beside the others.

The names this node answers, and the certificate the HTTPS listener serves each. A name with no certificate gets no HTTPS: its handshake is refused, and nothing asks an authority for one unless the name is set up here.
